question.text:
Let $\widehat{\,y}=\widehat{\,\beta}_0+\widehat{\,\beta}_1x=1-2.6x$ be the regression line fitted using a sample $(x_1,y_1), \: \ldots, \: (x_{11},y_{11})$ of $n=11$ paired observations. Assuming that all conditions for the simple regression model are satisfied, the mean square error of the model is $0.78,$ and $S_{xx} = \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 = 110,$ find a $95\%$ confidence interval for the slope of the regression line.

Hint: Use the fact that $P(T > 2.262) = 0.025,$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $9$ degrees of freedom. Also, the standard error for $\widehat{\,\beta}_1$ is given by \[ \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] = \sqrt{ \dfrac{\textrm{MSE}}{S_{xx}}}. \]
question.explanation:
We use the following notations:

  • $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ is the regression line that best fits the population, and

  • $\widehat{\,y}=\widehat{\,\beta}_0+\widehat{\,\beta}_1x$ is the estimate of the "true" regression line given by the data in our sample.

In this case, we have that

\[ \widehat{\,y}=\widehat{\,\beta}_0+\widehat{\,\beta}_1x=1-2.6x. \]

We are told that all assumptions for a simple regression model are held. So, given a value $\alpha$ between $0$ and $1,$ the corresponding $[100(1-\alpha)]\%$ confidence interval for the slope $\beta_1$ of our model can be written as

\[ \widehat{\,\beta}_1 \: \pm \: \overbrace{t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] }^{\textrm{margin of error}}. \]

Note the following:

  • $\!\widehat{\,\beta}_1$ is our point estimate for the slope, computed using the data points from our sample.

  • $P(T > t_{n-2,\alpha/2}) = \dfrac{\alpha}{2},$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $n-2$ degrees of freedom.

  • $\textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,]$ is the standard error of $\widehat{\,\beta}_1,$ given by \[ \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] = \sqrt{ \dfrac{\textrm{MSE}}{S_{xx}}} \] where we have:

    • $\textrm{MSE}$ is the mean squared error of the model: \[ \textrm{MSE} = \dfrac{1}{n-2}\sum\limits_{i=1}^n (y_i - \widehat{\,y}_i)^2 \] where $\widehat{\,y}_i$ is the estimate of $y_i$ given by our regression model.

    • $S_{xx}$ is the usual sum of squares formula: \[ \displaystyle S_{xx} = \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 \]

To construct the confidence interval, we proceed as follows:

  • Step 1. Find the point estimate. From the regression equation $\widehat{\,y}=1-2.6x,$ our point estimate is
    \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_1 = -2.6. \]

  • Step 2. Find the margin of error. Since we are interested in finding a $95\%$ confidence interval, we have \[ \alpha=1-0.95=0.05 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \dfrac{\alpha}{2}=0.025. \] We are given that $P(T > 2.262) = 0.025.$ As a result, \[ t_{n-2,\alpha/2} = t_{9,0.025} = 2.262. \] Now, we can compute the margin of error: \[ t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] = 2.262 \cdot \sqrt{\dfrac{0.78}{110}} \approx 0.2 \]

  • Step 3. Determine the limits of the confidence interval: \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_1 \: \pm \: t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] = -2.6 \pm 0.2 \]

question.text:
Production $\!$ ($x$) $24$ $27$ $30$ $31$
Price per $\mathrm{kg}$ ($ y$) $2$ $1.6$ $1.4$ $1.4$

The table above shows wheat production, in tons, and the average price of a kilogram of flour, in dollars, for a given country over the last four years. The corresponding linear regression line fitted using this sample is $\widehat{\,y} = 4 - 0.1x.$
Assuming that all conditions for the simple regression model are satisfied, $\overline{x}=28,$ and $\textrm{MSE}=0.007,$ find a $90\%$ confidence interval for the slope of the regression line.

Hint: Use the fact that $P(T > 2.92) = 0.05,$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $2$ degrees of freedom. Also, the standard error for the slope is given by \[ \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] = \sqrt{ \dfrac{\textrm{MSE}}{S_{xx}}}. \]

In this case, we have that

We are told that all assumptions for a simple regression model are held. So, given a value $\alpha$ between $0$ and $1,$ the corresponding $[100(1-\alpha)]\%$ confidence interval for the slope $\beta_1$ of our model can be written as

  • $\textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,]$ is the standard error of $\widehat{\,\beta}_1,$ given by \[ \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] = \sqrt{ \dfrac{\textrm{MSE}}{S_{xx}}} \] where we have:

    • $\textrm{MSE}$ is the mean squared error of the model: \[ \textrm{MSE} = \dfrac{1}{n-2}\sum\limits_{i=1}^n (y_i - \widehat{\,y}_i)^2 \] where $\widehat{\,y}_i$ is the estimate of $y_i$ given by our regression model.

    • $S_{xx}$ is the usual sum of squares formula: \[ \displaystyle S_{xx} = \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 \]

To construct the confidence interval, we proceed as follows:

  • Step 1. Find the point estimate. From the regression equation $\widehat{\,y}=4 - 0.1x,$ our point estimate is
    \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_1 = -0.1. \]

  • Step 2. Find the margin of error.

    • Since we are interested in finding a $90\%$ confidence interval, we have \[ \alpha=1-0.9=0.1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \dfrac{\alpha}{2}=0.05. \] We are given that $P(T > 2.92) = 0.05.$ As a result, \[ t_{n-2,\alpha/2} = t_{2,0.05} = 2.92. \]

  • $\widehat{\,y}=\widehat{\,\beta}_0+\widehat{\,\beta}_1x$ is the estimate of the "true" regression line given by the data in our sample.

In this case, we have that

\[ \widehat{\,y}=\widehat{\,\beta}_0+\widehat{\,\beta}_1x=12.7 - x. \]

We are told that all assumptions for a simple regression model are held. So, given a value $\alpha$ between $0$ and $1,$ the corresponding $[100(1-\alpha)]\%$ confidence interval for the slope $\beta_1$ of our model can be written as

\[ \widehat{\,\beta}_1 \: \pm \: \overbrace{t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] }^{\textrm{margin of error}}. \]

Note the following:

  • $\!\widehat{\,\beta}_1$ is our point estimate for the slope, computed using the data points from our sample.

  • $P(T > t_{n-2,\alpha/2}) = \dfrac{\alpha}{2},$ where $T$ has a student's $t$-distribution with $n-2$ degrees of freedom.

  • $\textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,]$ is the standard error of $\widehat{\,\beta}_1,$ given by \[ \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] = \sqrt{ \dfrac{\textrm{MSE}}{S_{xx}}} \] where we have:

    • $\textrm{MSE}$ is the mean squared error of the model: \[ \textrm{MSE} = \dfrac{1}{n-2}\sum\limits_{i=1}^n (y_i - \widehat{\,y}_i)^2 \] where $\widehat{\,y}_i$ is the estimate of $y_i$ given by our regression model.

    • $S_{xx}$ is the usual sum of squares formula: \[ \displaystyle S_{xx} = \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 \]

To construct the confidence interval, we proceed as follows:

  • Step 1. Find the point estimate. From the regression equation $\widehat{\,y}=12.7 - x,$ our point estimate is
    \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_1 = -1. \]

  • Step 2. Find the margin of error.

    • Since we are interested in finding a $90\%$ confidence interval, we have \[ \alpha=1-0.9=0.1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \dfrac{\alpha}{2}=0.05. \] We are given that $P(T > 2.92) = 0.05.$ As a result, \[ t_{n-2,\alpha/2} = t_{2,0.05} = 2.92. \]

    • Computing $S_{xx},$ we get \begin{align*} \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 &= (2-4.5)^2 + (4-4.5)^2 + (5-4.5)^2 + (7-4.5)^2 \\ &= 6.25 + 0.25 + 0.25 + 6.25 \\[5pt] &= 13. \end{align*}

    • Now, we can compute the margin of error: \[ t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] = 2.92 \cdot \sqrt{\dfrac{0.456}{13}} \approx 0.5 \]

  • Step 3. Determine the limits of the confidence interval: \[ \widehat{\,\beta}_1 \: \pm \: t_{n-2,\alpha/2} \cdot \textrm{SE}[\widehat{\,\beta}_1\,] = -1 \pm 0.5 \]
